answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to magnetohydrodynamic cell telemetry. Nodes authenticate by pumping saline electrolyte past a raven graphite sensor under pulsed magnetic fields to measure unique induced voltages. An attacker launching a tide of clones must fabricate discrete microfluidic chambers and coils per node, incurring steep hardware expenses. However, channel fouling drops signal fidelity to a nadir over time, occasionally rejecting valid agents.
